name: IsIsomorphic
input: s, t: strings of the same length
output: true if the characters of s can be replaced one-to-one to get t, else false

steps.note: Each character of s must always map to the same character of t, and no two characters of s may map to the same one, so check the mapping in both directions.

steps.hi: sToT, tToS <- two empty character maps
Walk s and t together; RETURN false at the first pair that contradicts either map, else record the pair
mid: FOR each position i of s
Let a be s[i] and b be t[i]
IF sToT maps a to something other than b, or tToS maps b to something other than a, THEN
RETURN false
Map a to b in sToT and b to a in tToS
lo: FOR i FROM 0 TO length of s - 1
IF (a is in sToT AND sToT[a] ≠ b) OR (b is in tToS AND tToS[b] ≠ a) THEN

steps.hi: RETURN true

name: CircularGameLosers
input: n: number of friends, numbered 1 to n clockwise
output: the friends who never receive the ball, in increasing order

steps.note: Number the seats 0 to n - 1. On turn p the ball moves p * k seats clockwise, so the next seat is (seat + p * k) mod n. The game ends at the first seat that gets the ball twice.

hi: visited <- no seat has had the ball yet
seat <- 0 (the ball starts there)
p <- 1 (the turn number)
lo: visited <- array of n false values

steps.hi: Pass the ball around the circle, marking each seat, until it reaches a seat that already had it
mid: WHILE seat is not yet marked in visited
Mark seat in visited
Move seat forward p * k places, wrapping past n - 1 back to 0
Add one to p

steps.hi: RETURN the 1-based numbers of the unvisited seats, in increasing order
lo: RETURN the list of i + 1 for each i FROM 0 TO n - 1 where visited[i] is false

name: LongestGoodSubarray
output: the length of the longest subarray in which every value occurs at most k times

steps.note: After adding nums[i], only nums[i] can occur more than k times, so shrink the window from the left until it does not; the window is then good.

hi: count <- empty frequency map of the window nums[left..i]
left <- 0
ans <- 0
lo: count <- empty map where a missing value counts as 0

steps.hi: FOR EACH index i and value x IN nums
lo: FOR EACH index i and value x IN nums

steps.hi: Add x to the window
Shrink the window from the left until x occurs at most k times
mid: WHILE the count of x is more than k
Decrement the count of nums[left]
Add one to left

steps.hi: ans <- max(ans, length of the window)
RETURN ans

name: MaxPizzaWeight
input: pizzas: array of weights; its length is a multiple of 4
output: the maximum total weight gained over all days

hi: Sort pizzas
days <- number of days; odd, even <- how many of them are odd and even days

steps.note: An odd day gains its heaviest pizza, so the odd days take the odd heaviest pizzas. An even day gains its second-heaviest pizza, so it uses the next two heaviest: the heavier one is that day's top pizza and the lighter one is the gain. The lightest pizzas fill the remaining slots.

steps.hi: ans <- sum of the odd heaviest pizzas
lo: ans <- sum of the last odd elements of pizzas

steps.hi: Add the lighter pizza of each of the next even pairs, going down from just below the odd heaviest
mid: Set i to the length of pizzas minus odd minus 2
REPEAT even times
Add pizzas[i] to ans
Subtract 2 from i

steps.hi: RETURN ans

name: PathSum
input: root: root of a binary tree (possibly empty)
output: the number of downward paths whose values sum to targetSum

steps.note: A downward path ending at a node sums to targetSum exactly when an earlier prefix sum on the root-to-node route equals (current prefix sum - targetSum). Count prefix sums for the current route only: add one on the way down, remove it on the way back up.

steps.hi: count <- how often each prefix sum occurs on the current route, starting with the empty prefix (sum 0, once)
lo: count <- map with count[0] = 1, where a missing sum counts as 0

steps.hi: DEFINE dfs(node, s), returning the number of target paths that end in node's subtree; s is the prefix sum above node
lo: DEFINE dfs(node, s), returning the number of target paths that end in node's subtree; s is the prefix sum above node

steps.hi: IF node is empty THEN RETURN 0
lo: IF node is null THEN RETURN 0

steps.hi: Count the target paths ending at node, using the prefix sums on the route above it
mid: Add node's value to s
Set ans to the count of the prefix sum s - targetSum

hi: Add s to the route's prefix sums
ans <- ans + dfs of both children
Remove s from the route's prefix sums
RETURN ans
lo: ans <- ans + dfs(node.left, s) + dfs(node.right, s)

steps.hi: RETURN dfs(root, 0)

name: WonderfulSubstrings
output: the number of substrings in which at most one letter occurs an odd number of times

steps.note: For each prefix, keep a 10-bit mask of which letters a..j have appeared an odd number of times. A substring is wonderful when its two endpoint masks are equal (no odd letter) or differ in exactly one bit (one odd letter).

hi: count <- how many earlier prefixes had each mask, starting with the empty prefix (mask 0, once)
mask <- 0
ans <- 0
lo: count <- map with count[0] = 1, where a missing mask counts as 0

steps.hi: FOR EACH letter c IN word
lo: FOR EACH letter c IN word

steps.hi: Add c to mask, then count earlier prefixes whose mask equals it or differs from it in one bit
mid: Flip the bit of c's alphabet position (a = 0) in mask
Add the count of mask to ans
FOR each bit b from 0 to 9
Add the count of mask with bit b flipped to ans
lo: mask <- mask with bit (position of c in the alphabet, a = 0) flipped
ans <- ans + count[mask with bit b flipped]

steps.hi: Record mask in count
RETURN ans

name: NetworkDelayTime
input: times: directed edges (u, v, t), travel time t from u to v
n: number of nodes, labeled 1 to n
output: the time until every node has the signal, or -1 if some node never gets it

steps.note: All times are nonnegative, so the unfinished node with the smallest tentative arrival time is final (Dijkstra). With n ≤ 100, finding it by scanning all nodes is fast enough.

hi: w <- n by n table of edge times, infinity where there is no edge
dist <- infinity for every node, except 0 for the source k
done <- no node is finished yet
lo: w <- n by n table of infinity
FOR EACH (u, v, t) IN times
dist <- array of n infinity values
done <- array of n false values

steps.hi: REPEAT n times
Finish the unfinished node u with the smallest dist, then shorten dist through u where that is faster
mid: Set u to -1 (no node chosen)
FOR each node j from 0 to n - 1
IF j is not done and (u is -1 or dist[j] is less than dist[u]) THEN set u to j
Mark u done
FOR each node j from 0 to n - 1
Set dist[j] to the smaller of dist[j] and dist[u] plus w[u][j]
lo: IF done[j] is false AND (u = -1 OR dist[j] < dist[u]) THEN u <- j

hi: ans <- the largest dist
RETURN -1 if ans is infinity (some node is unreachable), else ans
lo: IF ans is infinity THEN RETURN -1

name: MinimumTimeToEatGrains
input: hens: hen positions on a line
grains: grain positions on a line
output: the minimum number of seconds for the hens to eat every grain

steps.note: If every grain can be eaten within t seconds, it can also be eaten within any longer time, so binary search the smallest feasible t. To test a t, sort both lists and let the hens, from left to right, each eat the longest run of leftmost uneaten grains it can reach.

hi: Sort hens and grains
m <- number of grains
lo: Sort hens and grains in increasing order

steps.hi: DEFINE canFinish(t), returning whether every grain can be eaten within t seconds
lo: DEFINE canFinish(t), returning whether every grain can be eaten within t seconds

hi: j <- the first uneaten grain, starting at 0
FOR EACH hen position x, left to right
IF every grain is eaten THEN RETURN true
lo: IF j = m THEN RETURN true

hi: This hen eats the longest run of leftmost uneaten grains it can reach within t,
going left first or right first, whichever is cheaper; RETURN false if the first one is out of reach
mid: Let y be grains[j]
IF y is at or left of x THEN
Let d be x minus y
IF d is more than t THEN RETURN false
WHILE j is less than m and grains[j] is at or left of x
Add one to j
WHILE j is less than m and the smaller of d and (grains[j] minus x), plus (grains[j] minus y), is at most t
Add one to j
ELSE
WHILE j is less than m and grains[j] is at most t to the right of x
Add one to j
lo: IF d > t THEN RETURN false
WHILE j < m AND grains[j] <= x
WHILE j < m AND min(d, grains[j] - x) + grains[j] - y <= t
WHILE j < m AND grains[j] - x <= t

steps.hi: RETURN whether every grain was eaten

hi: Binary search the smallest t with canFinish(t) true, between 0 and an upper bound
(the bound: walk from the first hen to the first grain, then across all grains)
RETURN that t
lo: IF canFinish(mid) THEN high <- mid ELSE low <- mid + 1

name: MaxGridScore
output: the maximum sum of selected cells, with at most one cell per row and no repeated value

hi: rowsOf[x] <- the set of rows that contain value x (empty if none)
mx <- the largest value in grid
allRows <- the mask with every row
lo: rowsOf <- empty map where a missing value gives the empty set
FOR EACH row index i and row IN grid
FOR EACH value x IN row
m <- number of rows in grid
allRows <- mask with bits 0 to m - 1 set

steps.note: best[v][mask] = the best score using only values 1..v, each taken from a different row in mask. Each value is used at most once, so going value by value, either skip it or take it from one row in mask.

steps.hi: best <- table over values 0 to mx and all row masks, every entry 0
lo: best <- table with rows 0 to mx and one column for each mask from 0 to allRows, all 0

steps.hi: Fill best value by value: for every mask, either skip v or take it from one row of mask that contains v
mid: FOR each v from 1 to mx
FOR each mask from 0 to allRows
Copy best[v - 1][mask] into best[v][mask]
FOR each row r in rowsOf[v]
IF bit r of mask is 1 THEN
Raise best[v][mask] to best[v - 1][mask with bit r cleared] plus v, if that is larger
lo: FOR EACH row r IN rowsOf[v]
IF bit r of mask is 1 THEN
best[v][mask] <- max(best[v][mask], best[v - 1][mask with bit r cleared] + v)

steps.hi: RETURN the score for all values with every row allowed

name: MinPushBox
output: the minimum number of pushes to move the box onto the target, or -1 if impossible

hi: (si, sj), (bi, bj) <- the player cell and the box cell
isOpen(cell) <- the cell is inside the grid and not a wall
id(cell) <- one integer per cell, so a (player, box) pair can index a seen table
lo: isOpen(i, j) = (0 <= i < m AND 0 <= j < n AND grid[i][j] is not '#')
FOR EACH cell (i, j) IN grid

steps.note: A state is (player cell, box cell, pushes). Walking costs 0 pushes and pushing costs 1, so a double-ended queue that takes walks at the front and pushes at the back stays ordered by pushes (0-1 BFS).

hi: q <- deque holding the start state with 0 pushes
Mark (player, box) seen
lo: seen <- (m * n) by (m * n) table of false
q <- deque holding (id(si, sj), id(bi, bj), 0)

steps.hi: WHILE q is not empty
(si, sj), (bi, bj), pushes <- the state at the front of q, removed
lo: (s, b, pushes) <- remove from the left end of q
(si, sj) <- (s div n, s mod n)
(bi, bj) <- (b div n, b mod n)

steps.hi: IF the box is on the target THEN RETURN pushes

hi: FOR EACH of the 4 directions (di, dj)
(sx, sy) <- the player's next cell; skip it if it is not open
lo: FOR EACH (di, dj) IN up, right, down, left
IF NOT isOpen(sx, sy) THEN CONTINUE

hi: If the next cell is the box, push it (one more push, back of q);
otherwise walk there (same pushes, front of q); skip states already seen
mid: IF (sx, sy) is the box cell (bi, bj) THEN
Let (bx, by) be (bi + di, bj + dj)
Skip this direction if (bx, by) is not open or seen[id(sx, sy)][id(bx, by)] is true
Set seen[id(sx, sy)][id(bx, by)] to true
Append (id(sx, sy), id(bx, by), pushes + 1) to the right end of q
ELSE IF seen[id(sx, sy)][id(bi, bj)] is false THEN
Set seen[id(sx, sy)][id(bi, bj)] to true
Append (id(sx, sy), id(bi, bj), pushes) to the left end of q
lo: IF NOT isOpen(bx, by) OR seen[id(sx, sy)][id(bx, by)] THEN CONTINUE
Append (id(sx, sy), id(bx, by), pushes + 1) to the right end of q
ELSE IF NOT seen[id(sx, sy)][id(bi, bj)] THEN
Append (id(sx, sy), id(bi, bj), pushes) to the left end of q

steps.hi: RETURN -1
